facts.text: My left hand has become weak and I can't use it as well as before.

facts.item: weakness of the left hand: course
facts.text: It has slowly got worse over 5 years.
My fingers are numb.
It's in my thumb, index and middle fingers.
It started as mild numbness in my middle finger and over several years spread to my thumb and index finger.
My grip and pinch have become weak.
My symptoms don't bother me at night.

facts.item: earlier treatment for carpal tunnel syndrome
facts.text: At first the doctors thought it was carpal tunnel syndrome and treated it without surgery.
I've developed pain in my forearm.
It has been getting worse.

facts.item: inability to bend the thumb and index finger
facts.text: I've completely lost the strength to bend my thumb and index finger.

facts.item: wasting at the base of the thumb
facts.text: The fleshy part at the base of my left thumb has shrunk.
I can't work any more because of my hand.
I'm a chef.
I'm left-handed.
I haven't done heavy lifting.
I have a history of smoking.
I had cancer in my left breast.

facts.item: mastectomy and armpit lymph node removal
facts.text: My left breast was removed, along with the lymph nodes in my armpit.
I also had radiotherapy for the cancer.
I still take tamoxifen.

findings.name: inspection of the hand and forearm
findings.result: Marked wasting of the thenar eminence; subtle forearm muscle atrophy.

findings.name: sensory examination
findings.result: Reduced sensation in the thumb, index and middle fingers and in the thenar triangle.

findings.name: motor strength
findings.result: 0/5 strength in flexor pollicis longus, flexor digitorum profundus and flexor digitorum superficialis of the index finger.

findings.name: Tinel sign
findings.result: Elicited 12 cm distal to the medial epicondyle.

findings.name: nerve conduction studies and EMG
findings.result: No recordable median nerve motor responses on the left, with preserved sensory responses at the wrist. No evidence of widespread brachial plexus pathology or carpal tunnel syndrome; severe left median mononeuropathy with acute and chronic denervation.

aliases: median nerve entrapment at the pronator teres
median nerve compression by the pronator teres
gold.reasoning: 1. Carpal tunnel syndrome was initially considered because of radial-digit numbness but was excluded when “All provocative tests for CTS were negative.” 2. Brachial plexus pathology was considered but excluded as “No indication of widespread brachial plexus pathology and nor CTS was found.” 3. Struthers’ ligament entrapment was considered but excluded as “On bilateral humeral plain radiographs, no supracondylar processes (Struthers’ ligament origin) were identified, nor were any such palpable.” 4. Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome was considered given the motor paralysis but was unlikely since it “classically presents with pure motor weakness, as the AIN provides no cutaneous innervation.”
